description:
Make the first suite run after a crate-source change pass without profiled-fixture lock timeouts.

## Background

The profiled-repository fixture (`crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs`) is keyed on the package closure and the `jit` crate source digest, and is built in the suite on first use. When a source change produces a new key, the first consumer builds the fixture while the others wait up to `PROFILED_REPOSITORY_FIXTURE_LOCK_BOUND` (12 s) and then fail with "profiled-repository fixture … is busy". On a loaded host a cold build exceeds that bound, so the first `cargo-ci` after a source change fails several unit tests that pass on the warm cache. nextest's per-test timeout (`.config/nextest.toml`) caps any waiter at roughly 20 s, so raising the lock bound alone does not help. Runner setup hooks and per-test filters are out (they were removed deliberately).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A full suite run immediately after a crate-source change (cold fixture keys), on a host under load, passes with no fixture-lock "busy" failure; the evidence is recorded with the change.
- [hard] REQ-02: A consumer waiting on a fixture build fails only when its own build of that fixture fails, and reports that build's cause. A failed or dead holder does not fail a waiter; the waiter builds the fixture itself. A corrupt published entry fails its consumers, naming the entry.
- [hard] REQ-03: No runner setup hook, no per-test filter and no test-specific timeout is introduced.

## Evidence

Failing the real profiled fixture after its build (`68416fa02`): green 11.7 s, 4650 passed. Red under `cargo-ci`'s default fail-fast: 6.3 s, 7 failed, all with the cause. Red with `--no-fail-fast`: 16.3 s, 76 failed, 76 causes, 0 timeouts. With an artificial 5 s added per build: 21.4 s with 4 causes and 5 timeouts, and 81.6 s with 17 causes and 59 timeouts. A build takes about 0.1 s, against the 20 s limit. The failure-corpus fixture was not forced to fail, so these figures cover the profiled fixture only.

A red run shows a real cause when a build finishes inside the 20 s limit: the consumer holding the lock returns its build's error to its own test. A fixture build longer than that shows timeouts and no cause. If a fixture build approaches that limit, this is a defect to reopen.

`.config/nextest.toml` (`slow-timeout`, `terminate-after = 2`) ends a waiter under `Duration::MAX`: a scratch test blocked on it showed `TERMINATING [> 20.000s]`, then `TIMEOUT [20.004s]`.
title: Cold profiled-fixture builds no longer time out their waiters
